strengths: This paper proposes and studies a novel and interesting problem. It is pretty smart to consider the case where the cost of an arm could be negative.
The results are rich and good. It studies multiple cases, and provides good results for them. The results look good enough from my understanding and knowledge.
Well-motived model formulation. BwRK is an interesting extension of BwK, and the authors provide application examples as well (Sec. 6).
Algorithmic framework. The authors propose a primal-dual template (Alg. 1) that can be applied with various minimizers under different scenarios.
The problem setup is clearly motivated and introduced. The algorithm and analysis are thoroughly explained and neatly presented. Regret bounds improves on existing results.
This paper presents, for the first time, a best-of-both-worlds algorithmic design for bandits with replenishable knapsacks, accompanied by the corresponding theoretical analysis.

This paper provides the first instance-independent regret bound under i.i.d. inputs. This complements the earlier work of Kumar and Kleinberg (2022), which primarily focused on instance-dependent analysis in the initial BwRK paper.
weaknesses: It is not well discussed or stated how the negative cost could affect the problem. The paper lacks a discussion on whether standard primal‑dual approaches for BwK can be directly applied or if the negative costs require a fundamental change in the algorithmic design and analysis, and it needs concrete examples or counterexamples to demonstrate the limitations of existing methods.
The paper's writing and presenting need improvement. There are too many notations that could be avoided, and the definition of NextElement() is unclear, making the algorithm seem incomplete.

The theoretical results are not clearly discussed. It is unclear how tight the results are compared to known lower bounds; the paper should explicitly state those lower bounds and show how the proposed algorithm matches them.

Lack of experiments. The paper provides no empirical validation of the algorithm's performance, including comparisons to known baselines and analysis of how performance scales with problem parameters.

The paper lacks discussion of related work on bandits with (soft) constraints; the implications of negative c_t values on constraint satisfaction and connections to soft‑constrained bandit problems need more exploration.
There are some implicit assumptions that are not well justified, such as B = ω(T) and the resource range β ∈ [-1,0]; real‑world motivation and feasibility of these settings are unclear.
The Meta‑Algorithm appears to be a trivial extension of a prior work; the primary contribution compared with previous literature is not clarified.
The paper would benefit from the design of experiments to provide stronger empirical support for the theoretical findings.
